title: Alcotts and uncle Slater Brown's friendship with e.e. cummings
summary: The Alcott connection, then uncle William Slater Brown's ambulance corps friendship with cummings and the prison that led to The Enormous Room.

blocks.x: had not broken that up Thoreau would not have been able to build a cabin on a lake in Massachusetts, which of course produced the famous Walden. So that’s the second great book that the family created by inadvertence. There’s a third one actually. My grandmother’s cousin, I believe that’s the connection, Abigail May, married a lunatic, Bronson Alcott, who was responsible for creating a utopian colony called Fruitlands. And of course they scorned money and so nobody ever had any money and it was all a dreadful situation for everybody. And my family used to refer to her as poor cousin Abba because she married this very strange hippie basically was what he was. And so one of the daughters then, in order to save the family reputation, started writing books. And if it hadn’t been for that situation we never would have had Louisa May Alcott writing Little Women. So that was the third book that the family has created by inadvertence. And there’s actually a fourth one. My uncle, William Slater Brown, who liked to be known as Slater but was always known as Bill by the family and by most of the people that knew him, was a pacifist, had come to Columbia to study journalism, and in 1917, like a lot of young Americans, joined the Volunteer Ambulance Corps to go to France. He wouldn’t fight of course, as a pacifist, but to belong to an ambulance corps and help the French soldiers was a great — it was an adventure. And World War I, for that generation, was the adventure. These guys didn’t want to be left out, and so they would join the ambulance corps to go over there. So that’s what he did. And he was on a ship and they were just coming out of the New York harbor here and it was a little chilly, it was getting evening, and my uncle went down back to his cabin to get a jacket. And he came up and a friend of his, Red Lemon, who he joined up with, was sitting and talking with a young man who had come along and asked for a cigarette, a light for his cigarette. And so my uncle was introduced, this is Bill Brown, this is Estlin Cummings. And they became great pals, and spent much of their time in the ambulance corps together. And then my uncle wrote home some letters to my grandfather saying that the French army was in mutiny, which was the case. The French were of course trying to conceal this because they wanted the Americans to come in. This is just at the time the Americans had declared war. And so the French didn’t want to upset this so they were very disturbed that these letters were going back to the United States. They picked up my uncle and then they picked up Cummings because he was a friend. Now Cummings had done nothing, but Cummings would not say he loved the French better than the Germans and so they put him in jail and they put these two guys in this terrible prison in France, and kept them there. And eventually Cummings’ father was well connected and through pull he got out and went home, and my uncle stayed there and almost died. And there were finally more connections. Also my great uncle had been on Woodrow Wilson’s textile board, so they were able to make connections and get my uncle out and he came home, and Cummings’ © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

father wanted him to write up what had happened so that he could sue the U.S. government, and Cummings said he wasn’t going to have anything to do with that but that he would write it up as a compromise. So he and my uncle went up to Cummings’ place in New Hampshire and Cummings wrote a book which turned out to be The Enormous Room which was his first important book in the career of e.e. cummings. So that’s a fourth major book that the family has been responsible for by inadvertence.
That’s neat. You’ve been quite a catalyst.
So the members of my family, a lot of the members of my family were writers, but they really have not been much heard of. But by chance we were involved in some of these other things.
